chunks: Or have you taken a binding promise from Us which would hold till the Day of Judgement, that you will get whatever you demand?
ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'ayman 'alayna' mean in Surah Al-Qalam?
ai.summary: In this verse, Allah rhetorically questions the polytheists' assertion that He has a son or partners by invoking the idiom of 'oaths' (ayman) to signify binding covenants. Shia exegetes, such as Al-Tabarsi in *Majma' al-Bayan*, interpret this as a refutation of their claim that divine decree is contingent upon human opinion, emphasizing that God’s will is absolute and not bound by their false promises. The verse underscores the futility of their claim that God would fulfill whatever they dictate, highlighting His supreme autonomy.
